note: The sprite manifest. Every asset carries the full prompt it should be generated from, so the set can be regenerated identically by anyone with an account. The lighting rig in `rig` is baked into every prompt verbatim and must not be varied — it is the difference between a sprite sheet and a pile of unrelated pictures (docs/08-visual-design.md §6.6).
rig: Rendered as a miniature architectural model, a handcrafted diorama piece sitting on a flat base. Three-quarter view at 55 degrees elevation. Single warm key light from the upper left at 35 degrees elevation, soft cool ambient fill at 15 percent, short soft warm-neutral contact shadow beneath the base. Matte painted surfaces with visible handcraft texture, no gloss, no rim light. Muted earth palette: ochre, sage green, weathered stone, a touch of aged gold leaf. Isolated single object, plain flat neutral grey background, square framing, sharp throughout, no text, no people.
pipeline: images_generate with the subject line + rig
trim to content, record the base-centre anchor point
composite every finished sprite onto one test terrain plate
regenerate — never hand-correct — any asset whose shadow direction or warmth is off

anchors.note: Generated 2026-08-24 as the style lock. The chosen one becomes an `image` reference on every subsequent generation, which is what holds the style across 82 further assets.

landmarks.subject: A Neolithic ashmound of the South Indian Deccan — a low broad mound of pale grey vitrified cattle-dung ash, its surface crusted and cracked, ringed by a rough enclosure of upright timber posts and thorn brush forming a cattle pen.
A megalithic dolmen — four rough granite slabs standing as walls with a fifth vast capstone laid across them, a port-hole cut in the front slab, set on a low earth platform ringed with boulders.
An urn-burial field in the manner of Adichanallur — large red-slipped terracotta burial urns half-sunk in dry earth, some lidded, some tilted, with small offering pots beside them.
A Neolithic mudbrick compound — small rectangular rooms of hand-formed mudbrick with flat roofs and no windows, several compartmented storage cells, a few reed baskets against a wall.
An Indus granary block — a massive rectangular platform of fired brick with regular ventilation channels between raised sleeper walls, a loading ramp on one side.

The Great Bath of Mohenjo-daro — a rectangular watertight tank of finely fitted brick sealed with bitumen, steps descending at both ends, a colonnaded corridor around it, set at the highest point of a citadel platform.
A stepped stone reservoir in the manner of Dholavira — a deep rectangular rock-cut tank with tiers of steps descending on all four sides, a stone water channel entering at one corner.
The Lothal basin — a long rectangular baked-brick basin with a sluice gate at one end, a raised warehouse platform of brick cubes beside it, and a low quay wall.
A Painted Grey Ware village — a cluster of round wattle-and-daub huts with conical thatched roofs, a threshing floor, a cattle byre, and a few painted grey pots stacked outside.
A great earthen rampart in the manner of Kausambi — a huge sloping mud embankment faced with burnt brick, a timber palisade along its crest, and a gate passage cut through it.

An Ashokan pillar — a single tall polished sandstone monolith, slightly tapering, with a bell-shaped lotus capital carrying a seated lion, set on a low stone platform, its shaft covered in fine inscribed script.

A Buddhist stupa in the manner of Sanchi — a solid hemispherical dome on a circular drum, a square harmika railing at the summit with a triple stone parasol above it, encircled by a carved stone balustrade with a single ornate gateway.
A rock-cut cave portal in the manner of Barabar — a doorway cut into a granite hillside with a curved chaitya-arch lintel carved in imitation of timber, the interior walls polished to a mirror sheen.

A rock-cut chaitya hall facade in the manner of Karle — a great horseshoe-shaped arched window cut into a basalt cliff, a screen of carved pillars below it, and a free-standing lion pillar at the front.
A Gandharan vihara — a square monastic courtyard ringed by small cells, a stepped stupa at its centre with Corinthian-influenced pilasters, built of stacked schist slabs.
An Andhra stupa in the manner of Amaravati — a drum faced with carved white limestone panels, five free-standing pillars at each cardinal projection, a low railing of carved uprights and crossbars.
A Nalanda vihara block — a tall rectangular brick monastery of several storeys around a central court, ranks of identical cell doorways, a broad stair, and a brick temple tower beside it.
The Ajanta cliff — a curving horseshoe gorge of dark basalt with a row of cave openings cut into its face at one level, carved pillared verandahs and arched windows, a river below.
A tall slender wrought-iron pillar, unrusted, with a fluted bell capital, standing alone on a low stone plinth in a paved court.

The Ellora Kailasa — an entire temple carved downward out of a single basalt hillside, a tall tiered vimana, a flat-roofed hall, life-size elephants at the base, sunk within a rock courtyard cut on three sides.
The Kailasanatha at Kanchi — a modest sandstone temple with a pyramidal tower of few tiers, a row of small shrine cells around its courtyard wall, carved rearing lion pilasters.
A shore temple in the manner of Mahabalipuram — two stepped granite towers of unequal height rising directly from a rocky sea platform, weathered by salt, a low wall of seated bulls around it.

A cruciform brick monastery in the manner of Somapura — an immense square enclosure of monastic cells around a vast court, with a terraced cruciform temple rising in stepped stages at its centre, all in small red brick with moulded terracotta plaques.

A South Indian temple vimana in the manner of the Brihadeeswarar at Thanjavur — a tall stepped pyramidal tower of many diminishing tiers rising from a square sanctum base, each tier carved with miniature shrine niches, capped by a large octagonal stone cupola with a gilded finial.

A Chola temple in the manner of Gangaikondacholapuram — a vimana of concave curving profile, lower and broader than Thanjavur's, with a long pillared hall in front and a large stone Nandi bull facing it.
A Hoysala temple on a star-shaped plan — a low soapstone shrine whose plinth and walls zigzag in many points, every surface covered in dense fine carving, a squat tiered tower above.
The Konark sun temple as a stone chariot — a great sandstone hall on twelve pairs of enormous carved stone wheels, each wheel with ornate spokes and hub, teams of horses straining at the front.
An Odishan deul in the manner of Puri — a tall curvilinear tower of vertical ribbed bands rising to a flattened ribbed disc and finial, with a pyramid-roofed hall attached in front.

The Martand sun temple — a colonnaded courtyard of grey limestone with fluted Greek-influenced columns and trefoil arched niches, a central shrine with a steep pyramidal roof, mountains implied by the plinth.
A Dilwara Jain temple — a white marble shrine with a domed pillared hall, the dome carved into concentric rings of translucent lace-like pendants, an enclosing corridor of small identical cells.
A fortified gate in the manner of Sisupalgarh — a broad rampart of packed earth faced with laterite, a deep straight gate passage flanked by tall stone pillars, guard chambers to either side.
An Ahom paik village — raised bamboo-stilt houses with steep thatched roofs above a flooded paddy plain, a communal granary on posts, dugout canoes at the edge.
A Sultanate minar — a tall tapering tower of red sandstone in fluted and angled projections, ringed by projecting balconies on stone corbels, bands of inscribed calligraphy between them.
A Vijayanagara mandapa — an open pillared pavilion on a granite plinth, its piers carved as rearing horses and mythical beasts, a flat slab roof, boulders of the surrounding landscape at its base.

settlements.subject: Three small round huts of mud and thatch on bare earth, a fenced goat pen, a cooking fire.
A dozen mud huts with thatched roofs around a beaten central space, a well, grain baskets, a threshing floor.
Thirty mud-and-timber houses in loose rows with a small shrine, a tank of water, cattle byres and a boundary hedge.
A town with a long street of open-fronted shops under awnings, stacked goods, pack animals, a small temple tower at the end.
A compact town enclosed by a mud-brick wall with a single gate tower, tight rows of flat-roofed houses inside, a temple rising above them.
A harbour town — a stone quay with moored wooden sailing vessels, warehouses with tiled roofs, stacked bales and jars, a lighthouse beacon on a mole.
A dense city of flat-roofed brick houses on a grid of narrow streets, a large temple precinct with a tiered tower, a tank, and a market square.
A great city — concentric rings of streets around a vast walled temple precinct with a towering gateway, dense quarters of tiled roofs, a river with ghats along one edge.

agents.subject: A seated figure in simple undyed cloth, one hand raised mid-gesture, a small group seated on the ground before them, a fire between.
A standing figure in plain robes with eyes closed and one hand marking rhythm against the palm, no book, nothing written.
A seated figure bent over a palm-leaf folio on a low writing board, an iron stylus in hand, a stack of bound leaves and an ink pot beside.
A figure seated on a raised mat beneath a tree with four students cross-legged before them, palm-leaf bundles between.
A robed monastic figure walking with a shoulder satchel of manuscripts and a staff, sandals, shaved head.
Two seated figures facing one another across a low desk with two different manuscripts open, one pointing at a line.
A merchant caravan — four laden pack bullocks in file with bundled goods roped on, a driver walking at the head, a guard behind.
Two humped bullocks yoked and loaded with grain sacks and rolled cloth, standing at rest.
A flat-bottomed river boat of lashed timber with a single square sail and a steering oar, cargo jars amidships.
A coastal sailing vessel with a single raked mast and a triangular sail, sewn-plank hull, cargo lashed under matting.
A large ocean-going ship with two masts and square sails, a high stern, banks of oars, painted eyes at the prow.
Four foot soldiers in quilted cotton armour with long spears and hide shields, standing in a loose line.
A war elephant in painted caparison with a small platform on its back and a mahout at its neck.
Two mounted archers on small steppe horses, composite bows drawn, felt coats and fur-trimmed caps.

goods.subject: A coarse jute sack of wheat, mouth open, grain spilling at the base.
A tied sheaf of harvested rice stalks with the grain still on the ear.
A shallow woven basket heaped with small pale millet grain, a wooden scoop resting in it.
A tightly roped bale of raw cotton, fibres escaping at the corners.
An open sack of dried black peppercorns beside a small brass measuring cup.
Three rough-cut blocks of grey rock salt stacked on a reed mat.
Two bun-shaped copper ingots with rough cast surfaces, one propped against the other.
A dark porous lump of smelted iron bloom on a stone anvil, hammer scale around it.
A string of long polished orange carnelian beads, some etched with white line patterns, coiled on cloth.
A stack of white cut-shell bangles threaded on a cord, one broken.
Three rough chunks of deep blue lapis lazuli flecked with gold pyrite, on a linen square.
A folded bolt of lustrous woven silk in a deep dye, its edge unrolled.
A palm-leaf manuscript bundle — long narrow inscribed leaves stacked between two wooden covers and tied through with cord.
A rolled birch-bark scroll, edges frayed and curling, tied with plant fibre.
A stack of hand-made paper sheets under a stone weight, one sheet half-written.
A small heap of irregular silver punch-marked coins, each stamped with several small symbols.
A square steatite seal carved with an animal and a row of undeciphered signs, with a pierced boss on the back.

table.subject: A thick bound ledger book with a worn leather spine, lying closed on a wooden surface.
A low wooden manuscript chest with iron corner straps, lid raised, palm-leaf bundles stacked inside.
A small round earthenware ink pot with a stopper, ink staining its rim.
An iron writing stylus with a pointed end and a small blade at the other, lying on a palm leaf.
Six cubical chert weights of graded sizes arranged in a row on a flat stone.
A marked wooden measuring rod with incised graduations, resting across two blocks.
A thin sheet of clear glass in a plain brass frame with a small handle, lying flat.
A blank sheet of aged survey paper, slightly curled at the corners, held down by two small stones.
A shallow terracotta oil lamp with a pinched spout and a burning wick.
A small folded paper slip standing half-open, a line of handwriting on the visible face.
A blob of dark red wax pressed with a signet, still attached to a length of cord.
A rolled document tied with a faded ribbon, one end slightly unfurled.
